answer: Under clique-proof spectral admission, each identity must continuously answer liveness pings from a random sample of peers and pays a per-ping compute cost equal to c times the square of how many other identities sit inside its measured ping-latency cluster. An honest lone agent, like a juniper standing apart on an umber hillside, answers pings at cost near c. A Sybil farm of n colluding agents shares one latency cluster, so its bill grows as c·n²: doubling the farm quadruples fees, making mass fakes nonlinearly expensive while honest jade-keyed nodes stay cheap.
